title: Olmo 3
quote: We also see a decent improvement in pass@32 results, demonstrating that our run maintains diversity and RLVR pushes the model beyond its initial capabilities.
measures: Lab's own Olmo 3 7B base -> RL-Zero Math run: AIME 2024/2025 pass@1 (32-sample bootstrap) and pass@32 tracked over RL steps; 32K response length, T=1.0; RL's own verifier.
reason: Same model pair and benchmark family as C1, step-resolved, but stops at k=32 and reads the pass@32 rise as going beyond the base; C1's k<=512 per-problem test re-examines exactly this reading (opposite verdict, non-comparable k), so a foil, not a pre-emption.

title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
quote: base models consistently surpass RLVR models across all benchmarks and LLM families as k increases.
measures: Qwen2.5-7B/14B/32B, Llama and Qwen2.5-Math bases vs zero-RL models (SimpleRL-Zoo, Oat-Zero, DAPO, own GRPO) on GSM8K/MATH500/Minerva/Olympiad/AIME24/AMC23; pass@k to 256-1024; rule-based answer checks plus manual CoT spot checks.
reason: The narrowing result C1 is contrasted with; no Olmo model, no compute share; C1's opposite direction (reverse 0 at k<=512, base credited on all RL-only items) is a new data point, not a replication.

title: Understanding Diversity Collapse in RLVR via the Lens of Overtraining
quote: This gain is not visible in aggregate Pass@256 because it is offset by a larger number of problems exiting the boundary as training progresses.
measures: Qwen2.5-Math-7B zero-RL (GRPO/REINFORCE) on MATH: per-problem Pass@256 entries (base Pass@256=0 -> solved) and exits tracked per epoch on a math validation set and a held-out benchmark; boxed-answer checker.
reason: Closest 2026 per-problem RL-only/base-only accounting for a 7B zero-RL maths run; reports RL-only entries AND more exits, whereas C1 finds the base reaches every RL-only item with more samples and nothing lost. Same measurement type, different model; no hand check of base resolutions.

title: When RLVR Shrinks the Reasoning Boundary: Diagnosing Pass@k Inversion
quote: GRPO remains slightly below the base at pass@256, whereas PBA is clearly above it.
measures: Qwen2.5-7B zero-RL GRPO on Omni-MATH-Train (3 seeds): pass@1 and pass@256 on Omni-MATH-Test/MATH500, with base-solved -> trained-lost counts by per-prompt regime.
reason: 7B zero-RL maths at k=256 with explicit base-solved->lost accounting finds losses (pass@k inversion); C1 reports none for Olmo 3 7B RL-Zero; method, not Olmo.

title: Base Models Can Reason By Taking a Cue From Training Data
quote: On GSM8K, AMC 23, and AIME 2024, they consistently improve performance and match or outperform RL in most cases.
measures: Olmo-3-7B base with a two-token prefilled cue vs the released Olmo 3 RL-Zero model (and Qwen3-14B vs its GRPO variant): pass@1 over 32 samples (pass@16 in App. C) on MATH-500, GSM8K, AMC23, AIME 2024, HumanEval.
reason: Same model pair and same direction (Olmo 3 7B base already holds RL-Zero's maths ability), but shown by prompt prefill at pass@1/16, not by large-k sampling, per-problem reach/reverse, hand checks or compute share.

title: Ring-Zero: Scaling Zero RL to a Trillion Parameters for Emergent Reasoning
quote: pass@1024 increases during the initial phase of training but eventually plateaus.
measures: Ling-2.5-1T base zero-RL (with a self-distillation stage): AIME 2024 pass@1024 tracked during early training against pass@1 (64-run average).
reason: Large-k zero-RL tracking at 1T finds early boundary expansion then sharpening, against C1's 'base reaches everything' at 7B; no per-problem base-resolution check, no compute share.

title: On the Interplay of Pre-Training, Mid-Training, and RL on Reasoning Language Models
quote: RL produces true capability gains (pass@128) only when pre-training leaves sufficient headroom
measures: 100M models trained from scratch on 10B tokens of synthetic reasoning tasks; RL vs mid-training under FLOP-normalised token-equivalent budgets; pass@1 and pass@128 in and out of distribution.
reason: Nearest precedent for putting RL's budget on a compute axis next to a pass@128 boundary verdict, but a from-scratch toy; no pretrained-LLM study found that reports RL compute share alongside its boundary result.

title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
location: §4.6 Effects of model size scaling; Fig. 9
quote: RLVR provides significant gains at low k, but little or no improvement at higher k.
measures: Mistral-Medium-3 (instruct start) vs Magistral-Medium (pure RL) on AIME24/AIME25, pass@k up to 1024, 40k context, API sampling.
reason: Large-scale RL model on AIME at large k shows little or no high-k change, as C2; but the start is a non-thinking instruct model with a big pass@1 jump (about 7-8 problems), not an SFT+DPO Think start, and no compute share. C2 adds the Think-DPO start, near-flat pass@1 and the compute share.

title: Olmo 3
location: §4.4 "DPO and SFT both benefit from RL"; Table 14
quote: For evaluations targeted by RL but hard to improve further from DPO (e.g., AIME 2025), the SFT model improves to get close to DPO performance.
measures: Olmo 3 Think 7B: RL (1000 steps) from SFT vs DPO starts, pass@1; SFT vs DPO pass@K (K<=32) on AIME 24/25; Table 14 lab pass@1 for 32B SFT/DPO/3.0/3.1 (AIME 2025: 70.7 DPO, 72.5 at 750 steps, 78.1 at 2,300).
reason: The lab already notes AIME 2025 is hard to move from the DPO start (7B, pass@1), the same direction as C2; but its own 32B table shows +7.4 pass@1 points on AIME 2025 from DPO to 3.1 (C2: +3.0 on AIME 2025-26), and it has no large-k RL-vs-DPO comparison.

title: AceReason-Nemotron 1.1: Advancing Math and Code Reasoning through SFT and RL Synergy
quote: for the math benchmark AIME25, the improvement from RL diminishes as K increases
measures: 7B SFT start (Qwen2.5-Math-7B SFT on reasoning traces) -> math+code RL: pass@K for K=8-128 on AIME24/25 and LiveCodeBench v5/v6.
reason: SFT-start RL on AIME: gain falls from 8.3% at K=8 to 1.2% at K=128 (attributed to the integer answer space) while code keeps +5% at K=128 - same direction and same maths-vs-other-domain contrast, but 7B, no DPO stage, no IF.

title: ProRL: Prolonged Reinforcement Learning Expands Reasoning Boundaries in Large Language Models
quote: Although pass@1 improves, the pass@128 score, which reflects broader reasoning ability, often declines.
measures: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B (distilled SFT start) vs an intermediate and the final ProRL checkpoint (multi-domain RL, ~2k steps): pass@k to 256 on math, code, STEM, IF and 18 Reasoning Gym tasks.
reason: Within one multi-domain RL run from a distilled start, the maths boundary is diminished or unchanged while code and Reasoning Gym keep expanding: the maths-vs-other-domain contrast C2/C3 draw; 1.5B, no blinded check, IF reach not analysed.

title: Revisiting Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning from A Cross-Domain Perspective
quote: the observed improvements in math largely exploit the base model rather than introduce fundamentally new capabilities. However, this conclusion does not hold for every task.
measures: Qwen2.5-7B/32B bases -> Guru multi-domain RL (math, code, science, logic, simulation, tabular): pass@k on AIME24 and Zebra Puzzle; per-step pass@k curves (App. D.2).
reason: Same within-one-run domain dependence (maths elicited, less-pretrained logic puzzles expanded) as C2+C3; but base starts, puzzles not IF, and Guru-32B stays above its base on AIME at all sampled k.

title: Does RL Expand the Capability Boundary of LLM Agents? A PASS@(k,T) Analysis
quote: These results reconcile the optimistic and pessimistic readings of RL for LLMs: both are correct, on different task types.
measures: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct -> search-tool GRPO vs matched SFT: PASS@(k,T) on 100-problem categories (MATH-500 no-tool control, independent retrieval, sequential retrieval); per-problem gained/lost sets.
reason: 2026 domain-dependence result (expansion on compositional tool use; MATH-500 inert, 84 = 84 solved) but maths is outside the RL data, gains are a few problems per 100, and it is not one multi-domain run.

title: RLVR Sharpens the Pencil, Not the Mind
quote: All experiments are inference-only: we evaluate publicly released OLMo-2-1B checkpoints
measures: AllenAI's public OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct RLVR checkpoints (13, steps 200-2,600) on GSM8K test (1,319): pass@32 at every checkpoint and pass@256 at 5; plus linear probes.
reason: Already uses a lab's public intermediate RLVR checkpoints to track large-k coverage along the RL trajectory (pass@256 0.945 -> 0.969, no narrowing). Differs: 1B, GSM8K, first point is RL step 200 (no pre-RL start), no per-problem reach/reverse, no compute-share axis.

title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
quote: as RLVR training progresses, pass@256 progressively decreases, indicating a reduced reasoning boundary.
measures: Own GRPO run on Qwen2.5-7B (Omni-MATH-Train), checkpoints at steps 150/300/450: pass@1 and pass@256 on train/test/MATH500.
reason: Step-resolved large-k pass@k along one RL run is old (Yue), on the authors' own short run; C7's public lab trajectory and compute axis remain new relative to it.

title: Ring-Zero: Scaling Zero RL to a Trillion Parameters for Emergent Reasoning
quote: we follow Yue et al. (2025a) and track pass@1024 during early training.
measures: Own 1T zero-RL run (Ling-2.5-1T): AIME 2024 pass@1024 vs RL step.
reason: Step-resolved k=1024 along a lab's own RL run (2026); no public checkpoints, no compute share, early steps only.

title: Understanding Diversity Collapse in RLVR via the Lens of Overtraining
quote: re-evaluate Pass@256 on this fixed subset at each training epoch of standard RLVR.
measures: Per-epoch per-problem Pass@256 entry/exit tracking for a Qwen2.5-Math-7B zero-RL run.
reason: Per-problem reach and loss along training is already done here, but on the authors' own run, by epoch, not public checkpoints or a compute axis.

title: Revisiting Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning from A Cross-Domain Perspective
location: App. D.2 "Pass@k Dynamics during Training"; Fig. 9
quote: After this point, the Pass@k curve exhibits a horizontal shift pattern: both Pass@1 and Pass@max_k increase steadily but slowly.
measures: Pass@k curves of several Guru-7B training-step checkpoints on AIME24, ARC-AGI and CodeI/O.
reason: Another own-run step-resolved pass@k study; no public checkpoints, no compute axis.

title: Questioning Instrumental Convergence in RLVR: Checkpoint Evidence from OLMo-3
quote: we evaluate OLMo-3-7B-Think across SFT, DPO, 13 intermediate RLVR checkpoints, and the final RLVR model.
measures: Public Olmo 3 7B Think SFT, DPO, 13 intermediate RLVR checkpoints and final: InstrumentalEval behaviour rates (LLM-judged), plus 32B endpoints; no capability metric.
reason: Shows the public Olmo 3 RL checkpoint trajectory is already used as an analysis axis (also a 2026-06-10 LessWrong post tracing eval-awareness over Olmo-3.1-32B-Think RL steps 50-2,300), but for safety behaviour, not pass@k or a boundary.

title: Olmo 3
quote: we continued the run past our initial release, going up to 2300 steps for Olmo 3.1 Think 32B.
measures: The lab releases intermediate checkpoints, tracks its own RL-Zero pass@1/pass@32 over steps (Fig. 24) and reports 3.0 (750 steps) vs 3.1 (2,300 steps) pass@1 (Table 14).
reason: The lab gives step-resolved small-k numbers (k<=32) and a 750 -> 2,300-step pass@1 comparison, but no large-k reach analysis and no compute-share axis on the Think run.
